description: Reads one graph you saved earlier, by its graph_id, and returns the whole model in the same shape the run tools accept; an input saved without a distribution comes back with distribution_type null and distribution_params {}. Use this when you want to show the user what is in a saved model, edit it before running it again, or run it with run_monte_carlo_simulation, which takes the model inline and not a graph_id. To find a graph_id first, call list_graphs. It returns the graph_id, the name, when it was last updated, and the graph itself: its uncertain inputs with their distributions, the formula nodes, the links between them and the run settings. It reads the model, not any result of running it. It needs a Neumann account: send your key, or your signed-in token, in the Authorization header as a Bearer credential. No Neumann tool takes an api_key argument. Cost: free -- it debits no credits and spends none of your free daily runs -- but it needs an account; an anonymous caller gets authentication_required.

graph.description: The model itself, in the shape the run tools accept, except that an input saved without a distribution comes back with distribution_type null and distribution_params {}; such a graph cannot be run until you give that input a distribution. Each input comes back with its estimate (the range) beside its distribution_params; estimate.origin says whether the range was stated or worked out from the params. Edit it and pass it back to run_monte_carlo_simulation, or save the edited version with save_graph and this graph_id. Its full schema is run_monte_carlo_simulation's graph parameter.
